content.comment_body: Transferring programs from PC to [product_name] via ethernet works well, but I often need to send a program to a customer. Previously, with older [product_name] models, this was easy using the programming module (chip). Has [company_name] or anyone else introduced a device that lets you load a program onto a [version_no] model without a PC or network? I heard the SD card is mainly meant for data logging.
Hello [user_name], Here’s what the manual states: Regards,

Hi [user_name], I can copy the program from [product_name] to the SD card, but I can't manage a transfer going from PC to SD card to [product_name]. I tried saving a .lld as a .lsc with no success, and also tried changing the extension to .bin, but that didn’t work either.

Hi, In [product_name] software, open your program and use File/Save As. Choose "Binary dump (*.bin)" as the file type. The file must be named LOGO_U_P. Save it directly to the SD card, or send the file (unchanged name) to someone so they can copy it onto their SD card. Then you can use that SD card to load the program into a [version_no] model. See the attached example: Hope this helps.

That’s good, but now I’m seeing the error message ‘Card unknown Press ESC’. It’s the same SD card I've used for datalogging and reading/writing all day. I even tried a new 8GB SD card, with the same result. I can write to and read from the card, but transferring a .bin file from PC to SD card to [product_name] doesn’t work. UPDATE: After inserting the card and cycling the power, letting it read on startup, it appears to have read the card and the transfer menu worked. Does anyone know why this works only after power cycling? I'm glad it works, but curious about the reason.
It seems to work properly using the 'card' menu. You have to select the correct [product_name] type in the program (Standard vs. [version_no]).
Hi, Don’t remove or insert the SD card while [product_name] is running. Always perform a RUN/STOP/RUN sequence.
Thank you all, it's working great now!

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion focused on transferring programs to [version_no] models without a PC or network, revealing that SD card transfers require careful file formatting, specific steps, and sometimes power cycling. Users encountered confusion with error messages and correct procedures but identified that the process is more complex with newer models compared to past methods.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy and remote method for program transfer to [version_no] models, ideally replicating the simplicity of previous chip module solutions without needing a network, PC, or complex steps.
